records.deidentified_narrative: unit 1 was traveling south on n staples make a turn east onto lipan. it appears that cisneros (pedestrian) was in the crosswalk at lipan walking south to north when he was struck by unit 1. cisneros was transported by medics to spohn shoreline. the driver of unit 1 advised me that as he made the turn onto lipan he could not see as the sun shining directly in his eyes but stopped when he heard something impact the vehicle. after gathering information for this report i parked where i could observe the pedestrian signal which would have been applicable for the crossing of cisneros. i observed the traffic lights (vehicle and pedestrian) for approximately 15 minutes. it is evident to me that the indicator light for the pedestrian would operate only when the parallel vehicle traffic was on green and only after a pedestrian depressed the button indicating their presence and direction of travel. it is clear to me that unit 1 had a green light. it is unclear at this time what indicator was being displayed for the pedestrian. i drove to spohn shoreline where i observed cisneros laying on a gurney. i spoke with cisneros and asked him if he had used the button and he indicated that he was not sure but that he heard a beeping sound and believed that he had the walk indicator. injuries to cisneros were still unidentified at this time. i left cisneros with a slip of paper with the crash number (this report) and also my name and id number. no citation were issued at the time of this report.

records.public_safe_text: on saturday january 06, 2018 at approximately 2155 hrs. i, cpl. t. saavedra #10467 along with other officers responded to the area of [roadway]. to investigate a report of an auto vs. pedestrian accident. upon my arrival i observed ems on scene treating a male victim identified as raul calderon [date]. calderon advised he was walking his dog in the 600 blk of bandera when he was struck from behind by a vehicle. calderon stated he was walking in the grassy area the roadway when he was struck. calderon stated he did not get a good look at the vehicle since he was struck from behind. calderon complained of right sided head pain and right hip and upper thigh pain. calderon had swelling to the right front of his head and dried blood on the right side of his face and a small abrasion and redness to his right upper leg. witness jose ernesto martinez-vargas advised he did witness the impact, but heard it and observed the glare from calderon's phone screen as it flew through the air after calderon was struck. martinez-vargas described a gray, 4-door, passenger car with front right damage including the hood drove away from the scene. officers checked the area but were unable to locate the vehicle. the driver of the vehicle is at fault for failing to pass safely on [roadway] and failing to stop and render aid.

records.deidentified_narrative: on 01. 20. 2018 at approximately 1753 hours i was contacted by dispatch for a report by phone. i spoke to the caller, she stated at approximately 1230 hours on 01. 19. 2018 while she was picking someone up lower level terminal a by a2 pillar she was hit by a burgundy vehicle. caller stated as she was originally at pillar b18 but got a text message at 1228 hours from the lady she was picking up stating to come pick her up at a2. she drove around and upon arrival to pillar a2, she got out of her vehicle leaving her driver side door open then proceeded to go to the back of her vehicle to open the trunk. when she got done loading her vehicle as she started to walk towards her vehicle she felt the touch of a burgundy vehicle driven by an older man and occupied by a blonde hair passenger. caller [roadway] to a business meeting with her passenger so she departed and decided to call today. caller stated she was hit in her left hip and felt aches during the day today, [medical facility] tomorrow to be checked out. i reviewed the camera footage and saw the caller as she stated with her door open and loading luggages into her trunk. as she was behind her vehicle, three vehicles passed up next to her, the third vehicle appeared to match closely to the color of vehicle the caller stated hit her. i issued her a [case id] for this report over the phone. in my diagram illustration, the unknown burgundy vehicle will be listed as v1 while the caller's vehicle will be v2. v1 would be at fault for driver inattention, unknown make and model of the vehicle at this time. no further action taken by this officer.

records.public_safe_text: unit 1 was traveling northbound on [roadway]. unit 2, a pedestrian, was walking from east to west while in a clearly marked crosswalk. unit 1 driver stated the following: that unit 2 jumped out in front of his vehicle when the collision occurred. he estimated his speed at about 35-40 mph. witness 1 stated the following: that she was behind unit 2 walking westbound into the crosswalk. that she noticed unit 1 traveling southbound at i/o estimation of about 600 ft ([roadway] light pole north of intersection). she believes that there was plenty of distance in between unit 1 and the cross walk to proceed into the intersection. witness 2 stated the following: she to observed unit 1 traveling northbound at about the same distance of witness 1 statement, she also believed that there was plenty of time to proceed into the crosswalk safety. both witnesses were interviewed separately and both stated that they heard unit 1 engine with higher rpm as if he was accelerating just prior to the cross walk. unit 2 enters the crosswalk and traveled at about 34 feet where unit 1 collides front concentrated into unit 2 left side becoming vaulted to final rest at about 76 ft northeast of area of impact. unit 1 driver did not know what occurred when asked, and it is unknown what he was doing just prior to the collision. during i/o investigation, there was a clearly marked crosswalk intended for east/west travel for pedestrians. unit 1 stated that he was traveling at 35-40 mph. using time and distance formulas, unit 2 was walking in a crosswalk which would have taken unit 2 to travel 34 ft in about 5. 8 seconds which placed unit 1 at about 297 feet south of the crosswalk to travel in 5. 7 seconds. the roadway has a slight curve with a clear line of sight which there was not reason or obstructions for unit 1 not to see unit 2 enter the crosswalk. unit 1 failed to yield right of way to unit 2 colliding front concentrated to unit 2 left side. unit 1 secondary factor: unit 1 driver has not shown he has the skills or knowledge to safely operate a motor vehicle in a public roadway in the state of texas or union.
